noailles1558.summary: Three short passages in cipher inside a clear letter of Francois de Noailles, ambassador at Venice, to the Cardinal de Lorraine. Block A blames someone's 'bad order and poverty, or little conduct, that he gives to his affairs'; the subject is not in the cipher. Block B has someone who 'undertakes on him' and All Saints' Day; its opening signs are unread. Block C doubts that, for the singular pleasure and profit they have, 'they' come any bolder or better victualled; three stretches of it are open.
noailles1558.en:
A1  [for] the bad order and poverty-
A2  {?} [or] little {?} conduct that he gives to his
A3  affairs [?3 signs] [?]

"… on account of the bad order and poverty, [or] little conduct, that he gives to his affairs …" The subject is not in
the cipher; the clear text before it is about news from the Emperor's lands (see Charrière II, 505, where Noailles
writes on 7 Nov that the Emperor "still gives bad order to his affairs").

[Correction added 12 Nov 2026, not by Brackx: the phrase is on p. 505 of Charrière II, but in the letter headed "Venise, 7 et 20 octobre 1558", not in the letter of 7 Nov (Andrew Beling, beling/charrierecheck.md, confirmed on the OCR at the verification).]

B1  [?5 signs: the gloss has "…Seigneur"] undertakes, {?Monseigneur},
B2  on him, and the [?sign][?] AS [?sign] which {?is} the day
B3  [of] All Saints [?]

system: A homophonic alphabet of invented signs (76 distinct labels in 272 tokens) with three null signs and two word signs (qui, et), as recovered by Michael Brackx from the marginal decipherment of the time; a different alphabet from La Guiche's of 1551.
